question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Diversity in the Living World Practice Paper

sections.section_name: Section A (Comprehension & Knowledge - MCQs & Objective Items)

questions.question_text: Plants with soft, green, non-woody stems that are generally short in height are classified as:
Which plant type has a hard woody stem branching close to the base of the stem?
Weak-stemmed plants that spread horizontally along the surface of the ground are called:
Which anatomical structure connects a duck's toes to enable paddle-like swimming in water?
Mountain trees like Deodar have conical shapes and needle-like leaves primarily to:
options: B) Allow snow and rainwater to slide off easily
questions.correct_answer: B) Allow snow and rainwater to slide off easily

sections.section_name: Section B (Textual & Core Subject Application - 2 Marks)

questions.question_text: Differentiate between Climbers and Creepers with one example of each.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Climbers: Weak-stemmed plants that take external support to climb upwards (e.g. Pea, Money plant). (1 Mark)
2. Creepers: Weak-stemmed plants that spread horizontally along the ground (e.g. Pumpkin, Watermelon). (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: How do fish use their body shape and fins for efficient aquatic locomotion?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Streamlined Body: Tapered shape at both ends reduces fluid friction/drag while swimming. (1 Mark)
2. Fins & Tail: Flexible fins provide stability and propel/steer the fish through water. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: Describe the structural features of a tree trunk (bole).
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Main Stem: A thick, hard, dark woody main stem called a trunk or bole. (1 Mark)
2. Branching Pattern: Branches arise high above the ground level on the upper part of the stem. (1 Mark)

sections.section_name: Section C (Skill Items, Analytical Drills & Experiments - 3 Marks)

questions.question_text: Explain how desert cacti are structurally adapted to survive under extreme water scarcity.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Spines: Leaves modified into sharp spines drastically reduce water loss via transpiration. (1 Mark)
2. Fleshy Green Stem: Stem performs photosynthesis and stores water in thick waxy tissues. (1 Mark)
3. Deep Roots: Extensive root system penetrates deep soil layers to absorb groundwater. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: Describe a school garden survey method to classify local plants into Herbs, Shrubs, and Trees.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Measure plant height relative to human body (shorter, equal, much taller). (1 Mark)
2. Examine stem greenness and hardness (soft green vs hard woody). (1 Mark)
3. Note branching height (near ground base vs high up trunk) and record in a 3-column table. (1 Mark)

sections.section_name: Section D (Creative / Competency Case-Study / Multi-Step Analytical - 4 Marks)

questions.question_text:
Case Scenario: A botanist compares a Deodar pine from Himachal Pradesh with a Saguaro Cactus from Rajasthan.
(a) Identify the habitat of each plant. (1 Mark)
(b) Compare leaf structures and explain their functional adaptation. (1.5 Marks)
(c) What would happen if a Deodar tree were transplanted to a hot desert? (1.5 Marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Habitats: Deodar = Cold mountain region; Cactus = Hot arid desert. (1 Mark)
(b) Leaves: Deodar has needle-like leaves to shed snow; Cactus has spines to prevent transpiration water loss. (1.5 Marks)
(c) Transplantation: Deodar would suffer severe dehydration and heat stress due to high transpiration and lack of water storage tissues. (1.5 Marks)

questions.question_text:
Analyze animal locomotion across terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.
(a) Describe how bird forelimbs are modified for flight. (1 Mark)
(b) Explain how webbed feet aid ducks in swimming. (1 Mark)
(c) Differentiate between snake slithering and goat walking mechanisms. (2 Marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Bird forelimbs: Modified into feather-covered wings with hollow light bones for flight. (1 Mark)
(b) Webbed feet: Skin between toes expands like oars to push water backwards. (1 Mark)
(c) Locomotion: Snakes use flexible spine and ventral scales to slither in loops; Goats use four jointed limbs with hard hooves for terrestrial walking. (2 Marks)

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Diversity in the Living World Practice Paper

sections.section_name: Section A (Comprehension & Knowledge - MCQs & Objective Items)

questions.question_text: Which plant is an example of a Herb?
What type of stem does a pea plant possess that allows it to climb wooden stakes?
Which of the following organisms exhibits a streamlined body shape?
The habitat of an organism refers to its:
options: B) Natural living surroundings providing food, water, air, and shelter
questions.correct_answer: B) Natural living surroundings providing food, water, air, and shelter

questions.question_text: Which leaf modification is found in water lilies floating on ponds?
options: B) Broad flat leaves with waxy upper coating
questions.correct_answer: B) Broad flat leaves with waxy upper coating

sections.section_name: Section B (Textual & Core Subject Application - 2 Marks)

questions.question_text: Define 'Adaptation' and give one example from desert plants.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Adaptation: Presence of specific physical features or habits that enable an organism to survive in its habitat. (1 Mark)
2. Example: Cacti developing thick fleshy stems to store water in desert habitats. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: State two differences between a Shrub and a Tree.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Height: Shrubs are medium-height; Trees are tall. (1 Mark)
2. Stem Branching: Shrubs branch close to ground base; Trees branch high up on a main trunk. (1 Mark)

questions.question_text: How do community elders like Maniram Chacha contribute to understanding biodiversity?
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Traditional ecological knowledge regarding local plant uses, bird calls, and animal habits. (1 Mark)
2. Practical identification skills passed down through generations during nature walks. (1 Mark)

sections.section_name: Section C (Skill Items, Analytical Drills & Experiments - 3 Marks)

questions.question_text: Compare the root systems and leaf venation of monocot vs dicot plants.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Monocots: Parallel leaf venation and fibrous root system (e.g. Wheat, Grass). (1.5 Marks)
2. Dicots: Reticulate (net-like) leaf venation and taproot system (e.g. Mustard, Pea). (1.5 Marks)

questions.question_text: Explain how camels are adapted to survive in dry sandy desert habitats.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Wide padded feet prevent sinking into hot desert sand. (1 Mark)
2. Excretes concentrated urine and minimal sweat to conserve water. (1 Mark)
3. Long eyelashes and sealable nostrils block blowing desert sand. (1 Mark)

sections.section_name: Section D (Creative / Competency Case-Study / Multi-Step Analytical - 4 Marks)

questions.question_text:
Case Scenario: A student observes a pond ecosystem with Lotus plants, Fish, and Ducks.
(a) Identify the aquatic adaptations of Lotus stems. (1 Mark)
(b) Explain how fish gills extract oxygen from water. (1.5 Marks)
(c) Describe how ducks prevent their feathers from becoming waterlogged. (1.5 Marks)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Lotus stems: Long, hollow, light air-filled stems hold leaves floating at surface for sunlight. (1 Mark)
(b) Fish gills: Richly supplied with blood vessels that absorb dissolved oxygen as water flows over them. (1.5 Marks)
(c) Duck preening: Secretes waterproofing oil from preen gland spread over feathers. (1.5 Marks)

questions.question_text:
Design a 4-column Biodiversity Table for classifying garden plants.
(a) Specify the four column headers. (1 Mark)
(b) Enter details for Mint, Rose, and Neem tree. (2 Marks)
(c) Write a summary conclusion on plant structural diversity. (1 Mark)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
(a) Headers: Plant Name | Stem Nature (Green/Woody) | Branching Height | Category (Herb/Shrub/Tree). (1 Mark)
(b) Entries: 1. Mint (Green soft / Base / Herb); 2. Rose (Hard woody / Low base / Shrub); 3. Neem (Thick trunk / High bole / Tree). (2 Marks)
(c) Conclusion: Plants exhibit distinct growth habits adapted to light capture and support. (1 Mark)
